research_inputs.finding: Current serving systems emphasize continuous batching, prefix caching, structured outputs, tool calling, multimodal execution, and heterogeneous hardware plugins.
research_inputs.used_for: kept FAISAL’s control-plane contract provider-neutral and focused on deterministic admission rather than embedding a model runtime in kernel space

research_inputs.finding: MCP tools require schemas, deterministic listing is useful for caching, output schemas can be validated, and annotations are untrusted unless from trusted servers.
research_inputs.used_for: schema validation, deterministic ordering, output validation, and explicit annotation boundary

research_inputs.finding: MCP deployments must address confused deputy, token passthrough, SSRF, state-handle authorization, local-server compromise, and tool input/output controls.
research_inputs.used_for: caller-supplied scope policy and fail-closed contract validation; network execution remains outside this bounded module

research_inputs.finding: Production device management separates resource discovery, registration, health, allocation, and topology-aware scheduling.
research_inputs.used_for: preserving separation between contract admission and hardware/device qualification

limitations: This is a user-space control-plane validator and does not execute tools.
The bounded validator is not a complete JSON Schema implementation.
It does not establish external identity, OAuth token validity, or network egress safety by itself.
It does not qualify physical accelerators or production hardware.
It does not claim AGI, model quality, or production approval.
